title: Frictionless Route Germination - quick PRD seed
content:
Goal:
- Small, low-friction routing feature that lets apps opt into per-request cost/latency routing hints.
- Help product teams divert non-critical generation to cheaper model variants automatically while keeping a hard latency SLO for premium routes.

Top-level idea (one-liner):
- Add a tiny request-side schema (route_hint) and an opinionated server-side policy that maps hints to routing decisions (fast/cheap/isolated) with transparent metrics and a simple UI toggle in Console.

Why this matters (context):
- Several partners want predictable per-request economics. They give us a 95th percentile latency target and a monthly budget envelope and expect the platform to respect both.
- Current knob set (model variants, dedicated vs hosted) is blunt. Engineers end up building brittle client-side logic to route requests.
- If we standardize a tiny hint surface + server policy and provide sane defaults, we can reduce customer integration work and capture unit-economy wins (batching, caching).

Constraints / non-goals:
- Non-goal: full-featured policy language. Keep it tiny.
- Non-goal: replace Dedicated contracts. This targets Hosted and small Dedicated customers.
- Must not add per-request auth complexity. Keep API surface as minimal as possible.

Proposed request extension (sketch):
- route_hint: one of ["latency_sensitive", "cost_sensitive", "best_effort", "isolated"]
- optional: max_token_cost_cents (integer) — rarely used, advisory only
- optional: prefer_region (string) — advisory, used for data residency hints

Server policy sketch (defaults + overrides):
- latency_sensitive => prefer low-latency variant, pre-warm KV cache, route to regional pool if available
- cost_sensitive => route to quantized/cheaper variant, longer batch windows allowed, enable soft degradation in fidelity
- best_effort => allow lowest-cost path, asynchronous prefetch allowed, possible longer tail latency
- isolated => allocate to single-tenant or reserved pool (if available)

Metrics / observability needs:
- per-route_hint breakdown: p50/p95 latency, token cost, success/error rates
- delta vs baseline when hint is provided vs absent (to measure misuse)
- UI: simple toggle in Console to enable automatic mapping to model variants per workspace

User stories (draft):
- As a growth PM, I want free-tier calls marked as cost_sensitive so we automatically use cheaper variants and avoid surprises on the bill.
- As a product engineer, I want latency_sensitive paths to have extra tracing and guaranteed p95 < 300ms so my realtime feature stays snappy.
- As a security lead, I want isolated route to ensure requests with PHI go to Private/Dedicated pools.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API accepts route_hint and stores it in request metadata
- Routing policy engine maps hints to model variants with default rules (no console config required)
- Metrics collected and surfaced in Console (simple panel: traffic by hint, latency & cost)
- Basic server-side enforcement: cost_sensitive cannot be routed to Dedicated-only variants (safety check)

Rollout plan (quick):
- Internal dogfood: opt-in flag for Redwood Console workspace A/B test (week 1)
- Early access with 3 partners (instrument feedback, tune defaults) (week 2-4)
- Public beta + docs + SDK snippets (week 5-7)

Open questions / unknowns (todo):
- How to prevent clients from gaming hints (e.g., labeling everything latency_sensitive)? Need quota/backstop rules.
- Default mapping table — what model variants do we pick for cost_sensitive on each CPU/GPU region? (coord with applied-ml)
- Billing signals: do we show estimated-cost-per-request in responses or Console? UX trade.
- Isolated hint might require auth gating + enterprise-only license. License gating flow?

Implementation notes / rough tasks:
- API: small schema change in request proto + SDK layers (JS, Python) — add route_hint, backward compatible
- Serving-runtime: policy engine that runs before model selection, integrates with smart routing map
- Console: exposure panel + per-workspace default mapping UI (toggle + per-hint model map). Minimal first: toggle on/off + defaults.
- Metrics infra: add label route_hint to existing traces/metrics. Add cost per-token aggregation by hint.

Estimated effort (very rough):
- API + SDKs: 2 sprints (1 eng + 1 doc)
- Runtime policy + safety checks: 3 sprints (2 eng, small infra)
- Console metrics panel: 2 sprints (1 frontend, 1 design)
- E2E QA + partner rollouts: 1 sprint

Notes-to-self / possibilities:
- Could reuse existing "fallback" configs for best_effort path — just a thin mapping layer.
- Consider a soft-trust model: we accept route_hints but adjust routing based on historical client behavior (machine-checked trust score).
- Small UI: show % traffic labeled per hint to give customers visibility (helps curb overuse).

Quick sketches / prompts to add elsewhere:
- Jira epic idea: IF-ROUTE-HINTS (parent), stories: IF-ROUTE-HINTS-API, -RUNTIME, -CONSOLE, -METRICS, -SAFEGUARDS
- Slack thread seed: "route-hint proposal" with summary + ask for opinions from infra and applied-ml

Next steps (immediate):
- Pair with Mika to draft default mapping table (models x hint x region)
- Create Jira epic + initial tickets
- Quick UX mock for Console toggle (low fidelity)

Rough brainstorm fragments (choppy):
- "default to cost_sensitive for free-tier" vs "opt-in only" — tradeoff: cost vs surprise
- edge-case: multi-tool calls where one step is latency-sensitive and others best_effort — need per-call sub-hint? nope, too complex initially
- logging costs by hint helps build internal case for quantized model investments

References / related:
- convo: #product-onramp "latency ladder" (Jan 2025)
- doc: token-batching-hierarchy-journal (drive) — reuse batch window heuristics

-- end --

(quick, messy — save and iterate)
